# Hermes Optimizer - LLM reference

Hermes Optimizer is a reusable Hermes Agent skill that brings an install up to speed, or tunes an expensive one, without hardcoding one provider stack.

It runs a guided loop: read live configuration, ask only what inspection cannot answer, act in the Desktop app, checkpoint each phase, verify the result.

## Core principle
Ask first, infer second, optimize third.

## Modes
- Bring-up: fresh or messy install. Runs all seven phases.
- Tune: working install. Runs only the phases that audit dirty.

## The seven phases
0. Baseline audit - read-only, produces the honest baseline report
1. Provider and main model - Settings -> Models
2. Auxiliary and fallback routing - split lanes off the main model, add a real fallback
3. Plugins - Capabilities -> Plugins, install the baseline set matched to the user's work
4. Local utilities and document tooling - PDF and Markdown text extraction
5. Skills - Capabilities -> Skills, disable noise, keep real domains
6. Guardrails, checkpoints, safety - hard stop, checkpoints, smart approvals, audits
7. Verification and handoff - re-read, smoke-test, before/after

Every phase: questions, then actions, then a checkpoint. Never two phases at once.

## Anti-bloat rule
Never recommend a heavy local install that duplicates a capability already live.

Rejected by default: a multi-gigabyte local OCR model when the provider already has a working vision route; a local embedding model when the context engine already serves semantic recall; any local model duplicating a hosted route the user pays for; skills for platforms the host does not run.

Recommended by default: a document and data loader for PDF and Markdown (structured text extraction is the base layer, and hosted vision does not replace it); guardrails, checkpoints, and a real fallback chain; auxiliary routing that moves work off the premium main model; plugins that fill a genuine gap.

## Expected output shape
1. baseline audit, ranked by return
2. per-phase questions with concrete options
3. recommended lane mapping
4. rejections with stated reasons
5. verification notes

## Desktop surfaces
- Settings -> Models: main provider and default model
- Settings: auxiliary task rows and fallback models
- Capabilities -> Plugins: catalog install and enable
- Settings -> Plugins: per-plugin settings pages
- Capabilities -> Skills: enable and disable
- Capabilities -> Connectors: MCP and connectors

CLI is for reading state, verifying, and what the app has no field for.

## Safety rules
- do not present one user's model stack as a public default
- prefer disabling skills over deleting bundled skills
- state the enabled-versus-installed skill counts, they differ
- detect providers and reachable models from live state before asking the user to list anything
- verify routes with real calls, a picker entry is not proof of a live route
- keep examples generic in public documentation
- never write umbrella auxiliary keys (heavy/medium/light), the Desktop page does not parse them
